# `supabase/security-definer-function`: SECURITY DEFINER function callable through the API

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family   | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                    |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| supabase | medium           | 5.5                      | [CWE-269](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html), [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

Functions in exposed schemas declared `SECURITY DEFINER` that API clients can call with
`supabase.rpc()`: callable by `anon` (the default unless `EXECUTE` is revoked) or by any
logged-in user. Reported at **medium** severity when `anon` can call it and **low** when
only logged-in users can, always with low confidence because the body is not analysed.

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

Functions in an exposed schema can be called by API clients with supabase.rpc(). A SECURITY DEFINER function runs as its owner and ignores RLS. Unless it checks auth.uid() itself, any caller can make it act on anyone's data.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- Function {function} is SECURITY DEFINER in an exposed schema and callable by anonymous clients via rpc(); it bypasses Row Level Security.
- Function {function} is SECURITY DEFINER in an exposed schema and callable by any logged-in user via rpc(); it bypasses Row Level Security.

## How to fix

Prefer SECURITY INVOKER. If definer rights are required, put the function in a non-exposed schema, or revoke EXECUTE from public, anon and authenticated and call it from the server. Inside the function, check auth.uid() and set search_path = ''.

### Vulnerable

```sql
create function public.delete_user(uid uuid) returns void
language sql security definer as $$
  delete from auth.users where id = uid;
$$;
```

### Fixed

```sql
create function private.delete_user(uid uuid) returns void
language plpgsql security definer set search_path = '' as $$
begin
  if uid is distinct from (select auth.uid()) then
    raise exception 'not allowed';
  end if;
  delete from auth.users where id = uid;
end $$;
revoke execute on function private.delete_user(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Functions that check the caller themselves** (`auth.uid()` inside the body) can be
  safe. VibeGuard does not prove the check is correct, so they are still reported. Confirm
  it and suppress with the reason.
- **Trigger functions** and functions with `EXECUTE` revoked from `anon`, `authenticated`
  and `public` are not callable through the API and are not reported.
- **Recommended pattern:** keep `SECURITY DEFINER` functions in a schema that is not
  exposed, set `search_path`, and `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, public`.
- **Limitations:** function bodies are not executed or fully analysed.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```sql
-- vibeguard-ignore-next-line supabase/security-definer-function -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the statement VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  supabase/security-definer-function: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-269](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html): Improper Privilege Management
- [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html): Improper Access Control
